title: Nuclear Fission and Chain Reactions
text: Nuclear fission is a nuclear reaction in which a heavy atomic nucleus splits into two or more smaller nuclei, releasing a large amount of energy. The most commonly fissioned isotopes are uranium-235 and plutonium-239. When a neutron strikes a fissile nucleus, it can cause the nucleus to split, releasing additional neutrons that can trigger further fissions in a self-sustaining chain reaction. This principle underlies both nuclear power plants and nuclear weapons. In power plants, the chain reaction is controlled to produce steady heat, which is converted to electricity via steam turbines.
